answer: Keystroke cadence gives each agent a fingerprint that costs real human time to fake. The operator types normally for 14 days while the system records hold times and gaps between keys, building a timing signature from 2,000 keystrokes. Random rechecks ask for a fresh phrase within 10 minutes, and a mismatch locks the identity and burns its 200 POA bond. An attacker needs a different typist per fake identity, about $30 each, so 1,000 fakes cost $30,000. Like grain in cedar or a vein in jade, no two signatures match, and copying one is like bees hunting nectar from a single flower.
